idea: Workplace design consultancy for finance firms
buyer: COOs at funds and boutique banks fitting out offices
pain: Generic office design that ignores how trading and research floors actually work
v1: A workplace strategy for one fund's office move
verdict: A genuine crossover with a solvent buyer - the rare architecture idea aimed at people with money.

why.distribution: Warm fund contacts, though office moves are infrequent and unpredictable events.
why.demand: Inferred; firms do pay for workplace strategy, usually to established practices.
why.fmf: An architect who has sat on a research floor knows what those spaces need better than any designer.
why.revenue_structure: One project per client per decade.
why.defensibility: The combination is genuinely rare and the sector knowledge compounds.
why.time_to_revenue: Waiting for an office move: 3-6 months.
why.tailwind: Flat; hybrid working has reduced fit-out volumes.
why.ceiling: £22k x 9 projects = £198k, but nine finance office moves reaching her in a year is implausible.

ceiling_arithmetic: £22k x 9 projects = £198k. Office moves are once-a-decade events per firm; nine in one year from a 50-firm network is implausible. Realistic: 1-2 = £22-44k.
carries: Aimed at a buyer who can actually pay, with a genuinely scarce dual perspective.
kills: Event frequency. The trigger is an office move, which she cannot create or predict.
test: Ask five fund contacts whether they are moving or refitting in the next 18 months.
test_fail: None are - which is the likely answer.
